title: TS SDK stream proxy: typed frame sniffing and consumer handback ergonomics
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Design and implement a lightweight proxy layer in the TypeScript SDK that unifies AsyncIterator and Web Streams consumers by doing typed frame sniffing and providing ergonomic handback semantics. This ticket covers the API contract, an incremental implementation that preserves backpressure and cancellation semantics, and examples for customer-facing docs.
context: We currently expose both AsyncIterator and ReadableStream shapes for streaming responses. Customers repeatedly hit friction when switching between consumers because of subtle differences in cancellation propagation, backpressure, and typed chunk framing (e.g., tokens vs. control frames like done/error/meta). Several support cases and internal PRs show ad-hoc shims in example code; we need a first-class, documented proxy that: 1) transparently converts between AsyncIterator and Web Streams, 2) preserves abort signal propagation, 3) performs light typed-frame decoding (string|json|frame) without forcing allocations, and 4) offers an explicit handback API for dual-consumer scenarios where caller needs to re-emit a frame downstream.
proposed_solution: Introduce `StreamProxy` in the TypeScript SDK runtime: a tiny object that receives raw stream frames from the runtime, classifies frames as {type: 'data'|'meta'|'control'}, and exposes two ergonomic surfaces: `asAsyncIterator()` and `asReadableStream()` plus an advanced `handback()` method allowing the consumer to return a frame to the origin stream or to a side-channel. Key design goals: maintain native backpressure (do not buffer unbounded), ensure AbortSignal/throw-on-abort semantics match underlying platform, and preserve typed framing semantics so structured outputs (JSON chunks, function calls) remain first-class.
implementation_notes:
Phased rollout to minimize SDK churn:
1) Define TypeScript types for Frame: union of {type, seq, value, meta?}. Keep runtime wire format identical.
2) Implement `StreamProxy` thin wrapper around existing AsyncIterator<RawChunk> consumer in hosted runtime client that performs synchronous classification and yields typed frames.
3) Implement `asReadableStream()` backed by a TransformStream which consumes the proxy's iterator and enqueues typed frames, honoring backpressure via controller.desiredSize and properly reacting to controller.close()/controller.error().
4) Implement `handback()` as an awaitable that writes into a small bounded MPSC queue the runtime will read from; expose a feature flag to the control plane until full integration done.
5) Add cancellation tests that assert AbortSignal passed to `asAsyncIterator()` propagates to runtime cancel endpoint and that `ReadableStream.cancel()` triggers iterator return.
6) Add TS/JS examples in repo and end-to-end test that hooks a fake runtime server to verify frame ordering and retry handback route is invoked.
Notes: avoid copying whole chunk into JS if value is ArrayBuffer/Uint8Array when possible; use transferable arrays in worker scenarios. Keep footprint small (single extra closure per stream).
acceptance_criteria:
1) `StreamProxy.asAsyncIterator()` and `asReadableStream()` are exported in SDK and pass unit + e2e tests for backpressure and cancellation.
2) `handback()` is implemented with an opt-in feature flag; E2E test shows the runtime receives the handback and re-enqueues the frame to fallback route.
3) Documentation page with two usage examples (iterator + ReadableStream) and a migration note for existing customers appears in docs site.
4) Performance regression < 2% in p99 latency for existing streaming workloads in canary.
5) No memory leak in long-lived streams (>10k tokens) in stress tests.
testing_plan: Unit tests for Frame classifier, iterator-to-stream conversion, and handback queue semantics. Integration test using sdk-testkit fake runtime: simulate sequences containing data/meta/control frames, assert final consumer order, backpressure behavior by delaying reads, and abort propagation. Load test with 200 concurrent streams for 30 minutes to detect leaks and GC pressure. Add instrumentation to CI to capture event loop delays and heap growth.
risks_and_mitigation:
Risk: handback could be abused to create unbounded buffering. Mitigation: bounded queue with configurable limit (default 16 frames) and a policy to reject new handbacks with an explicit error or back-pressure signal.
Risk: differences between Node and browser ReadableStream behavior. Mitigation: keep separate small adapter for each platform and run browser-based tests (Playwright).
Risk: tight coupling to runtime wire format. Mitigation: keep Frame classifier isolated; add feature-flagged schema negotiation header.
rollout_plan:
1) Merge behind feature flag `stream_proxy_v1` and ship to nightly.
2) Run canary on small tenant set + internal infra-testing for 72h with enhanced metrics.
3) Remove feature flag after 2 weeks and opt-out window.
4) Publish docs, update examples, and notify customers via changelog.
